display.purpose: The brand statement over camera 01. One per page.

title.purpose: Product name in the product view.

wordmark.purpose: VULT LABEL in the top bar and bag head; the footer repeats it as a giant mark.

body.purpose: Descriptions and notes, tabular numerals on.

lede.purpose: Opening paragraph of the information band.

label.purpose: Form labels, size legend, log terms, bag row labels.

osd.purpose: Camera ids, clocks and feed captions, with the hard black outline.

osd-price.purpose: Product price in the product view.

osd-tag.purpose: The 'Motion' tab on the motion-detection box, black on OSD White.

shadows.name: osd-outline
shadows.purpose: text-shadow stroke on all camera lettering; the OSD's native outline.

shadows.name: track-keyline
shadows.purpose: Black stroke on the motion box's 2px OSD White frame (the tag takes 0 0 0 1px #000). Zero offset, zero blur.

shadows.name: recorder-edge
shadows.purpose: Bezel line of the recorder panel against the rack.

shadows.name: statement-lift
shadows.purpose: text-shadow under the display statement on the hero feed only.

shadows.name: vault-door-cast
shadows.purpose: The physical vault door at the entry gate.

motion.name: go-live
motion.purpose: Colour returning to a feed's subject and the live crop to scale(1.06).

motion.name: camera-cut
motion.purpose: Product view opening from a horizontal slit (clip-path inset 49% to 0).

motion.name: cam-zoom
motion.purpose: Product view stage zooming in from scale(0.5); dropped on lost feeds.

motion.name: track-lock
motion.purpose: Motion box growing onto its target from scale(0.8); 0.12s delay on tiles, 0.6s in the product view, 0.2s steps(2) at the vault door.

motion.name: track-drift
motion.purpose: Motion box jitter of a few pixels in the product view.

motion.name: timecode-frames
motion.purpose: Frame count on timecode clocks; clocks otherwise tick on the second.

motion.name: scan-roll
motion.purpose: One scan roll over the hero on load.

motion.name: vault-swing
motion.purpose: The vault door opening; the one smooth physical movement.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Removes drift, grain movement, scan roll, REC blink, tile crop, motion box animations, camera cut, zoom, timecode frames, dial shake and door transitions.

components.name: Toast

narrative.overview:
The store is the vault's security system. Visitors watch the vault on CCTV: the label speaks in on-screen display lettering over live, grainy grey feeds, and the shop is a monitor wall where every product is a camera. Around the feeds the world is poured concrete: a pale grey ground, near-black ink, hairline and two-pixel rules, square corners everywhere. Nothing is decorated that a security rig would not show.

The system runs on one deliberate light theme. The concrete is the room; the dark rack behind the monitor wall and the dark vault gate are places inside that room, not a dark mode. There is no theme switch and no `prefers-color-scheme` branch (`color-scheme: light`). Density is high and terse: a voice set in a heavy, extra-wide grotesk, product facts in camera lettering, very few words.

Motion is video, not interface. Nearly every transition and animation is quantised with `steps()`: grain jitters, the hero camera drifts in 160 discrete steps, a single scan roll passes on load, the REC dot blinks hard, a live camera crops in on its subject, the motion-detection box locks onto a target, timecode counts frames at 25 per second, and opening a product cuts from a horizontal slit to fullscreen and zooms the camera in. The one smooth movement is the physical vault door swinging open on entry. Reduced motion removes drift, grain movement, the roll, the blink, the crop, the box animations, the cut, the zoom and the frame count.

The finish review judged this world at its ceiling after the monitor wall gained its main feed, recorder panel, timecode, zoom and motion detection. Future work extends the world's existing devices; it does not add new kinds of camera furniture.
keyCharacteristics: Pale concrete ground, grey feeds, white on-screen lettering with a hard black outline.
Two typefaces with separate jobs: Archivo for voice and labels, VT323 for camera lettering and data.
Square corners on every surface and control; circles only for the REC dot and the vault dial.
Garments show desaturated until their feed is selected.
The camera system's own instruments as the only ornament: timecode, zoom readout, motion-detection box, the recorder panel.
Stepped, video-like timing; one smooth exception for the vault door.
A single light theme by design.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Saturated red belongs to the recording system: the REC dot, and the small marker that flags a fault. Prices, sale states, CTAs and scarcity never turn red.

rules.name: The Concrete Room Rule
rules.body: One light theme. Dark grounds (the rack, the vault gate, lost feeds, the hero feed) are places in the world, entered and left; they are never a global dark mode.

rules.name: The Two Jobs Rule
rules.body: Archivo speaks; VT323 reports. VT323 appears only as on-screen camera lettering (camera labels, clocks and timecode, "No signal", the zoom readout, the motion tag, the recorder panel, the dial numerals) and as data (prices, stock, quantities, sizes chosen in the bag, subtotals, toasts). Headings, body copy, buttons and form labels are always Archivo. In a row that pairs a label with a value, the label is Archivo and the value is VT323.

rules.name: The Wide Voice Rule
rules.body: Every Archivo heading is weight 900 at width 112% or 125%, uppercase, with negative tracking. Every Archivo label is 750 to 800, width 112%, uppercase, with positive tracking. Body text is the only Archivo set at normal width and mixed case.

rules.name: The Picture Holds The Depth Rule
rules.body: Shadows, vignettes and grain belong to the camera image and the vault itself. Panels, buttons, chips, the drawer and the toast stay flat. The keylines on the REC dot, the motion box and the recorder panel are strokes, never offset or blurred.

dos: **Do** set prices, stock, quantities, subtotals and every camera label in VT323; set every heading, label, button and sentence in Archivo.
**Do** put the hard black OSD outline on all white lettering that sits on a camera picture.
**Do** keep every control and panel square (0px) and draw structure with 1px and 2px Ink rules.

**Do** quantise motion with `steps()` and remove drift, grain movement, the scan roll, the REC blink, the tile crop, the motion box animations, the camera cut, the zoom and the timecode frame count under reduced motion.
**Do** show a garment greyscale until its feed is hovered, focused or opened.
**Do** show sold-out pieces as lost signal from real stock, never as a red badge.
**Do** keep the first camera as the wall's main feed and close the wall with the recorder panel.
**Do** run timecode frames only while the clock is on screen, and tick every clock on the second.
**Do** put scroll offsets on the content (`scroll-margin-top: var(--bar-h)` on main and footer targets), never on the bar or the root.
donts: **Don't** add a dark theme or a theme toggle; the system is one light concrete world.
